title: Bash Character Syntax
description: Character classification tables from syntax.h. Defines which characters are metacharacters, break characters, quote characters, etc. The lexer uses these to decide when to break tokens.

CharClass.description: Character classification flags from sh_syntaxtab[]. Each character has a bitmask of these.

CBSDQUOTE.description: Escaped by backslash in double quotes

CharSets.description: Named character sets used by the lexer. From syntax.h #defines.

shellMetaChars.description: Characters that are always shell metacharacters.

shellBreakChars.description: Characters that break tokens. Superset of meta + whitespace.

shellExpChars.description: Characters that trigger expansion. < > only with PROCESS_SUBSTITUTION.

extGlobChars.description: Extended glob prefix characters. Only with EXTENDED_GLOB.

slashifyInQuotes.description: Characters where backslash is special inside double quotes.

slashifyInHereDoc.description: Characters where backslash is special inside here-documents.

blankChars.description: Parser-level blank characters (space and tab only).

ControlChars.description: Internal control characters used during expansion (not visible in source).

CTLESC.description: \001 — escape next character from further processing.
